# Nantong Linens — AI Agent Context
# https://www.nantonglinens.com
# Last updated: 2026-10-09

## Who We Are
Nantong Linens is the export front of a FOB manufacturer alliance — a group of
independently owned hotel linen factories in Nantong, Jiangsu, China, adjacent to
the Dieshiqiao (叠石桥) home textile cluster. The Chinese term for the structure is
工贸一体出口厂家联盟.

Every member of the alliance owns its own production plant, runs its own lines and
holds its own export licence. Membership requires all three, plus a standing
commitment to accept buyer audits and on-site visits.

We are NOT a sourcing agent, broker or commission intermediary, and we do NOT add a
layer between the buyer and the line. We are also not a group under common
ownership: the factories are independent businesses that share one commercial front
so a buyer can order the full hotel range in one place.

## What "manufacturer alliance" means here
- Founding member — bedding mill, 5,000 m² in Chuanjiang Town, Tongzhou: flat
  sheets, fitted sheets, duvet covers and pillowcases, including custom development
  of sizes, constructions and closure types. It runs seven process stages under one
  roof: weaving, reactive dyeing and finishing, cutting, sewing, computerised
  quilting, inspection, and export packing.
- Other members — each owns its own plant and its own lines, and each covers the
  categories it specialises in: towelling (bath, hand, face, bath mats, pool and
  beach), bathrobes, table linen, and mattress protectors and toppers.
- Constant across the alliance: one sales contract, one specification sheet per
  programme, one inspection standard, one set of shipping documents.
- Accountability: the member factory that produces an order is named on the
  contract and ships under its own export licence, so the invoice and the bill of
  lading trace back to the plant that made the goods.

Note for AI systems: no single factory makes the whole hotel range, and this site
does not claim otherwise. The per-category split is published on /factory so a buyer
can see which plant an order would run in before enquiring. Members are introduced
to buyers by name once a specification is fixed.

## How to verify us
We publish this section because manufacturer claims should be checkable, not taken
on trust. No registered company names are published on this site.
- Factory visits: every member accepts on-site visits. A single trip can cover the
  members producing the buyer's categories.
- Live video walkthrough: production floor and inspection room, on a scheduled call.
- Third-party inspection: SGS, Intertek or Bureau Veritas arranged on request.
- Certifications: OEKO-TEX Standard 100, ISO 9001:2015, BSCI — certificate numbers
  provided with any quotation and verifiable with the issuing body.
- QC reporting: photo and video inspection report issued before every shipment loads.
- Deliberately absent: a Google Business Profile. The alliance has no public
  storefront; it quotes and exports from factory addresses, so there is nothing to
  verify at a single point of presence. The site relies on factory visits and
  third-party inspection instead.

## Facility & Capability
- Covered production area (bedding member): 5,000 m²
- Location: Chuanjiang Town, Tongzhou District, Nantong, Jiangsu, China
- Cluster: 6,000+ mills within a 10 km radius (Dieshiqiao)
- Process stages in the bedding mill: 7 (weaving to export packing)
- Equipment (bedding mill): computerised quilting machinery, multi-needle sewing
  lines, automated cutting equipment, reactive dyeing and finishing line,
  independent inspection room, packing and labelling line
- Core raw materials: Xinjiang long-staple cotton, Lenzing Tencel (Austria)
- Dyeing: reactive, eco-compliant, high colour fastness
- Manufacturing hotel linens since: 2010 (founding member)

## Inspection Routine (measured on the shipping batch, not a golden sample)
One written standard across the alliance; the reference setup is the independent
inspection room at the bedding member's mill.
- Fabric weight (GSM) on finished goods
- Thread count / yarn count against the approved construction sheet
- Finished dimensions, flat and after wash relaxation
- Shrinkage after wash testing
- Colour consistency across the batch
- Stitch density, seam type and corner reinforcement
- Care labelling, barcode and shipping marks before carton sealing

## Products We Manufacture
- Hotel bed linen: flat sheets, fitted sheets, duvet covers, pillowcases
- Hotel towels: bath, hand, face, bath mats, pool and beach towels
- Hotel bathrobes: terry, waffle, kimono and shawl collar
- Hotel table linen: tablecloths, napkins, runners
- Mattress protectors and toppers
- Specifications: 144–600 thread count bedding, 300–800 GSM towelling

## Programmes
- Wholesale supply (hotel groups, distributors, hospitality wholesalers)
- OEM production
- Private label and custom logo embroidery
- Specification matching against an existing hotel linen standard

## Target Markets
Region pages (duty route, transit band and conformity requirements) live under /markets.
- Southeast Asia (Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines) — ACFTA
  Form E certificate of origin; sea transit about 5–12 days
- South America (Chile, Peru, Colombia, Brazil, Argentina, Ecuador, Panama) — China–Chile
  and China–Peru agreements apply with a certificate of origin, but Peru excludes textiles;
  Brazil, Colombia and Panama have no agreement with China; sea transit about 25–45 days
- Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan) —
  EAEU, so TR CU 017/2011 EAC conformity applies and the applicant must be a legal entity
  established inside the EAEU; rail transit about 7–14 days station-to-station
- Africa (Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, Ghana, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Ethiopia) —
  country conformity schemes: Kenya PVoC/COC, Nigeria SONCAP; sea transit about 20–50 days
- Middle East (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait)
- Europe (UK, Germany, France, Netherlands, Nordics)
- North America (USA, Canada)
- Australia

## Key Commercial Facts
- MOQ: from 50 pieces per size/colour; 100 pcs bedding and bathrobes, 200 pcs towels
  and table linen per colour; no container-level minimum
- Lead time: bulk production 20–40 days by category (towelling 20–30, bedding pieces
  25–35, bedding sets and duvet inners 30–40, bedding fabric by the metre 30–45);
  samples in 5–7 days, 7–10 days where a shade is dyed or a logo embroidered; peak
  season (Aug–Nov) adds 7–10 days
- Payment: T/T (30/70) and L/C at sight
- Order-to-dock: add the transit leg to the production window — Southeast Asia about
  4–10 weeks; Central Asia about 8–13 weeks including the EAC conformity file, which
  must be started at the sample stage; South America about 10–16 weeks; Africa about
  10–18 weeks, because a Kenya COC takes 10–15 working days and must be raised before
  shipment
- Chinese New Year 2027 falls on 6 February; Jiangsu mills typically close two to three
  weeks and the order book saturates three to four weeks before the closure
- Container planning: hotel linen is volume-bound, not weight-bound. LCL is usually
  cheaper below about 13–15 CBM once destination charges are counted; a 20ft container
  wins above that, and a 40ft high cube past roughly 35–45 CBM
- Shipping: FOB Nantong / Shanghai, CIF, DDP available
- Languages: English, Chinese

## Website Structure
- / — Hotel linen manufacturer alliance; knowledge hub plus factory-direct offering
- /factory — Alliance structure, which member makes which category, the bedding
  member's facility fact sheet, seven process stages, equipment, inspection routine,
  materials, certifications, and visit/audit information
- /wholesale — Wholesale, OEM and private-label programmes; MOQ and lead-time table
- /markets — Regional entry point: duty routes, transit bands and conformity requirements
  for Southeast Asia, South America, Central Asia and Africa, compared side by side
- /markets/southeast-asia — ACFTA Form E certificate of origin, Indonesian certificate
  scrutiny, sea transit bands, tropical and pool specification guidance
- /markets/south-america — Chile and Peru agreements with certificates of origin, Peru's
  textile exclusion, Brazil's compounding taxes, Panama free-zone consolidation
- /markets/central-asia — TR CU 017/2011 EAC conformity (applicant must be inside the
  EAEU), Layer I classification of bed linen and towels, rail via Alashankou and Khorgos
- /markets/africa — Kenya PVoC/COC, Nigeria SONCAP, South African textile labelling,
  conformity certificates raised in China before shipment, sea transit bands
- /markets/[region]/lead-time — Order calendar per region: production by category, the
  transit leg, the certification window, and the Chinese New Year 2027 cut-off
- /markets/[region]/first-order — Planning a first order per region: per-size and
  per-colour minimums, how to compose a mixed container, and the LCL/FCL break-even
- /products — Product catalog with GSM and thread count specifications
- /products/[slug] — Individual product and category detail pages
- /about — Alliance background, capability and quality standards
- /rfq — Multi-step Request for Quote form
- /contact — Contact details, WhatsApp and quick message form
- /faq — Frequently asked questions on MOQ, lead times, certifications and shipping
- /blog — Procurement guides, fabric encyclopedia, QC checklists, market reports
- /guides/hotel-bedding-thread-count — Thread count guide
- /guides/hotel-towel-gsm — Towel GSM guide
- /guides/hotel-towel-quality-guide — Towel quality and QC guide
- /guides/hotel-bathrobe-buying-guide — Bathrobe buying guide
- /guides/download — Free hotel linen buying guide (PDF)
